report.title: The State of AI: How Organizations Are Rewiring to Capture Value

figures.title: Share of organizations using AI, and gen AI, in at least one business function
figures.subtitle: Respondents to McKinsey's Global Survey on the state of AI, 2017 to 2025; the latest point comes from 1,491 participants in 101 nations surveyed 16-31 July 2024
figures.quote: Organizations' use of AI has accelerated markedly in the past year, after years of little meaningful change. Organizations that use AI in at least 1 business function, % of respondents
figures.note: Survey self-report, not an administrative count: a respondent saying their organization has 'adopted' AI in one function can mean anything from a few employees experimenting to embedded redesigned processes - McKinsey states it deliberately left 'adopted' undefined. The definition of AI use also changed twice (in 2017 it meant AI in a core part of the business or at scale; 2018-19 meant embedding at least one AI capability; since 2020 it means adoption in at least one function), so the early points are not comparable with the later ones. The x-axis is labelled by publication year, so the '2025' point is the survey fielded 16-31 July 2024. Data are weighted by each respondent's nation's contribution to global GDP. The gen AI series begins in 2023.

figures.title: Share of organizations regularly using gen AI in at least one business function, by industry
figures.subtitle: Respondents whose organizations regularly use gen AI, by the respondent's industry; global survey of 1,491 participants, 16-31 July 2024
figures.quote: Business functions in which respondents' organizations are regularly using gen AI, by industry, % of respondents ... Using gen AI in at least 1 function
figures.note: Self-reported by individual respondents about their own organizations; 'regularly using' is undefined and a single team's use counts for the whole organization. Industry base sizes are small and uneven, so cross-industry gaps of a few points are not meaningful: technology n=199, business/legal/professional services n=179, media and telecom n=77, advanced industries n=97, financial services n=193, consumer goods and retail n=111, healthcare/pharma/medical products n=113, energy and materials n=142. 'Overall' is the full 1,491-respondent sample, weighted by national GDP.

figures.title: Share of respondents reporting a revenue increase in the business unit using gen AI, by function
figures.subtitle: Respondents whose organizations regularly use gen AI in the given function; first-half 2024 survey (fielded 22 Feb - 5 Mar 2024) compared with second-half 2024 survey (16-31 July 2024)
figures.quote: Organizations increasingly see gen AI's effects on revenues in the business units using the technology. Revenue increase within business units from gen AI use, past 12 months, by function, % of respondents
figures.note: Survey perception, not measured revenue: respondents are estimating the revenue effect of gen AI on their own unit, with no accounting basis and no control for what would have happened anyway. Values are the totals printed at the end of each stacked bar, summing three bands (increase by more than 10%, 6-10%, and 5% or less); segments may not sum exactly to the printed total because of rounding. Asked only of those reporting regular gen AI use in that function, so the base differs by function and by wave; respondents saying 'no change', 'decreased revenue', 'don't know' or 'not applicable', and functions that are cost centres, are excluded. McKinsey notes elsewhere in the same report that more than 80% of respondents say their organizations see no tangible effect on enterprise-level EBIT.

figures.title: Share of respondents reporting a cost decrease in the business unit using gen AI, by function
figures.subtitle: Respondents whose organizations use gen AI in the given function; first-half 2024 survey (fielded 22 Feb - 5 Mar 2024) compared with second-half 2024 survey (16-31 July 2024)
figures.quote: Respondents increasingly report cost reductions from gen AI within business units using the technology. Cost decrease within business units from gen AI use, past 12 months, by function, % of respondents
figures.note: Self-reported perception of cost change within a business unit, not audited cost data, and not net of what gen AI itself cost to build and run. Values are the totals printed at the end of each stacked bar, summing three bands; segments may not sum exactly to the printed total because of rounding. The band definitions differ slightly between the two waves (first half: 20% or more / 10-19% / under 10%; second half: 20% or more / 11-19% / 10% or less), so the two series are not perfectly like-for-like. Asked only of those reporting gen AI use in that function; 'cost increase', 'no change', 'not applicable' and 'don't know' are excluded, and manufacturing is omitted because the base was too small to report.

figures.title: Expected change in a business function's headcount over three years as a result of gen AI use
figures.subtitle: All functions combined ('Overall' row); respondents whose organizations use gen AI in the given function, global survey of 1,491 participants, 16-31 July 2024
figures.quote: Expected change in business function's number of employees as a result of gen AI use, next 3 years, % of respondents reporting gen AI use in the given function
figures.note: This is a forecast of intent, not an employment outcome: respondents are predicting their own function's headcount three years out, and such predictions have no track record here to check against. Asked only of respondents reporting gen AI use in the given function, so it excludes organizations not using it. Figures may not sum to 100% because of rounding. The 12% 'don't know / not applicable' share is large enough to move the picture on its own.

figures.title: Types of content organizations generate with gen AI
figures.subtitle: Respondents whose organizations regularly use gen AI in at least one function; global survey of 1,491 participants, 16-31 July 2024
figures.quote: While text is the type of content that organizations are most commonly creating with gen AI, they are also experimenting with other modalities. Types of content generated by gen AI at respondents' organizations, % of respondents
figures.note: Self-reported and multiple-select, so the shares do not sum to 100. Asked only of respondents whose organizations regularly use gen AI in at least one function, and calculated after removing those who said 'don't know'. It records that a modality is being generated somewhere in the organization, not how much of it, at what quality, or whether it reaches a customer.

figures.title: How centralized each element of AI deployment is
figures.subtitle: Respondents whose organizations use AI in at least one function (n = 1,229); global survey fielded 16-31 July 2024
figures.quote: Risk and data governance are two of the most centralized elements of deploying AI solutions, whereas tech talent is often hybrid. Degree of centralization of AI deployment, % of respondents
figures.note: Self-reported organizational structure from 1,229 respondents whose organizations use AI; figures were calculated after removing the share who said 'don't know / not applicable', so they describe only those with a view. A respondent's read of how centralized their own company is can differ from another respondent's at the same company. Each element's three shares sum to 100%.
